Article Title: Tesla reports $1.53 billion in free cash flow amid one-fifth cut to 2026 spending forecast
Article Text:
Tesla cuts 2026 capex by one fifth

SpaceX merger puts Tesla's spending under scrutiny

Revenue beats estimates, but net income plunges 43%

FSD adoption and automotive margins improve

Tesla reported an unexpected $1.53 billion in free cash flow in the third quarter, beating Wall Street's expectations, as the electric vehicle maker spent less than anticipated on capital expenditure.However, a one-fifth cut to its 2026 spending forecast has raised questions about its investment plans for artificial intelligence (AI), robotics and autonomous driving. The company now expects capital expenditure of around $20 billion in 2026, down from its earlier forecast of more than $25 billion. Tesla did not specify which areas would see lower spending.In the quarter ended September 30, Tesla spent $4.7 billion on capital expenditure, double the amount spent a year earlier but well below the $7.5 billion analysts had expected on average, according to LSEG data.The lower spending helped Tesla report free cash flow of $1.53 billion, compared with market expectations of a cash outflow of $4.92 billion.Tesla's shares initially rose 2% in after-hours trading after the results, supported by positive free cash flow, higher gross margins and revenue that exceeded Wall Street expectations. However, the stock reversed direction to trade 2% lower. Shares have fallen around 14% this year."The free cash flow beat was a pleasant surprise, but when combined with the lower-than-expected capex, raises questions on the next step for the automaker," said Ryan Lee, senior vice president of product and strategy at Direxion, which offers exchange-traded funds tied to Tesla. "Lower capex suggests less of an 'all-in' approach to the AI arms race than one would expect from Elon."The results come as chief executive Elon Musk explores a potential combination of Tesla and SpaceX, his space venture. The unexpected cash generation could strengthen Tesla's financial position ahead of a possible deal, but lower investment in AI, robotaxis and humanoid robots could raise concerns about its ability to deliver on its growth ambitions.On Tuesday, Musk described a merger between the two companies as a "good idea" and said they had formed special committees to discuss the proposal. He declined to provide further details during Wednesday's conference call with analysts.A combination would bring together businesses central to Musk's long-term vision of an integrated technology and manufacturing group spanning AI, energy, robotics, communications and transportation on Earth and beyond.However, investors will want to see whether Tesla is investing enough to turn Musk's ambitions into commercial businesses, particularly as the robotaxi rollout has lagged behind his promises."The merger still faces a high bar, but tonight’s numbers make the financial logic harder to ignore," said Thomas Monteiro, a senior analyst at Investing.com."The main takeaway is that Tesla's surprisingly positive cash flow quarter did not come from stronger profits, but from spending billions less than planned at a time when SpaceX is preparing to invest up to $40 billion in a single quarter."Tesla's financial performance presented a mixed picture. Revenue remained flat compared with a year earlier, despite the end of US tax credits that had supported sales in the previous year. Nevertheless, the figure exceeded Wall Street's expectations.Net income fell 43% during the quarter.Tesla said it had ended the quarter with its largest backlog of passenger vehicles in four years. Higher petrol prices have supported demand for electric vehicles, particularly in Europe.The company delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter, putting it on track to increase annual deliveries for the first time in three years."Demand is growing rapidly for our vehicles. It's exceeding our production by a significant margin," Musk said on the conference call with analysts. "In a nutshell, after many years of sort of grind and things being fairly flat, I think we're now headed for a lot of fun and significant growth."Tesla also reported stronger adoption of its driver-assistance technology in North America. The FSD (supervised) attach rate exceeded three-quarters of new vehicle deliveries, an increase of nearly 20 percentage points from the second quarter, the company said.Automotive gross margin, excluding regulatory credits, reached 18.1% in the third quarter, above analysts' estimate of 16.7%, according to Visible Alpha data.Tesla's energy business has recently helped offset pressures on its automotive operations. The latter remain under scrutiny as competitors worldwide launch newer, often cheaper models. Tesla continues to rely heavily on its ageing Model 3 and Model Y.Despite the competitive pressures, Tesla aims to produce five million vehicles annually by around 2030, compared with an expected 2.5 million this year.
Article Summary: Tesla reports $1.53 billion in free cash flow, beating Wall Street's expectations. Company cuts 2026 capex forecast by one fifth to $20 billion, down from $25 billion. Results come as CEO Elon Musk explores a potential combination of Tesla and SpaceX.

Article Title: Rupee falls 3 paise in early trade as crude soars beyond $115 per barrel
Article Text:
Rupee falls in opening trade

NEW Delhi: Rupee began the week on a negative note, falling 5 paise to 94.98 against US dollar in early trade. Rising crude oil prices and growing tensions in the Middle East put pressure on the currency, while a weaker dollar and lower US Treasury yields helped limit the fall.The currency opened at 94.92 in the interbank forex market before slipping to 94.98. This followed a 12-paise fall on Friday, when it closed at 94.93 against the dollar, marking its second straight day of losses.Forex traders said that growing uncertainty over the Middle East conflict weighed on the rupee. High oil prices and selling by foreign investors could add to the pressure, while a weaker dollar and possible intervention by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) may offer some support.Anuj Choudhary, research analyst at Mirae Asset Sharekhan, told PTI “The Indian rupee opened slightly lower on elevated crude oil prices and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. However, softness in the US Dollar and US treasury yields cushioned the downside.""We expect the rupee to trade with a slight negative bias on risk aversion in global markets amid escalation of tensions in the Middle East. Elevated crude oil prices and selling pressure by FIIs may also pressurise the rupee.However, weak US Dollar and any fresh intervention by the RBI may support the rupee at lower levels," Choudhary added.The dollar index, which measures the US currency against six major currencies, fell 0.15% to 101.49. However, this was not enough to prevent the rupee from declining.Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, rose 1.92% to $114.48 per barrel in futures trade.Dalal Street also opened lower, with the Sensex falling 536.30 points to 72,583.86 and the Nifty declining 200.10 points to 22,402.80. Last week on Friday, foreign institutional investors (FIIs) bought Indian shares worth Rs 887.65 crore, according to exchange data. India's foreign exchange reserves fell by $5.011 billion to $721.016 billion in the week ended October 16, according to Reserve Bank of India data released on Friday.This followed a larger decline of $8.578 billion in the previous week, when reserves stood at $726.027 billion.
Article Summary: Rupee falls 5 paise to 94.98 against US dollar in early trade. Rising crude oil prices and growing tensions in the Middle East put pressure on the currency. A weaker dollar and lower US Treasury yields helped limit the fall. India's foreign exchange reserves fell by $5.011 billion to $721.016 billion.

Article Title: Bank holiday on Valmiki Jayanti 2026: Will banks remain shut on October 26? Check state-wise list
Article Text:
Bank holiday on October 26

Where are banks closed on October 26?

Upcoming bank holidays in October 2026

October 29:

October 31:

Which banking operations will be affected?

NEW DELHI: India’s festive calendar continues to bring a series of holidays in October, making it important for bank customers to check the schedule before heading to a branch. On Monday, October 26, banks will remain closed in selected states for Laxmi Puja, Accession Day and Maharishi Valmiki’s birthday.While bank holidays vary across states depending on regional festivals and observances, customers planning branch visits should check whether their local branch is operating. Those looking to make large cash deposits, process cheques, obtain demand drafts or complete other branch-dependent work may need to plan their visits around the holiday schedule to avoid an unnecessary trip.Banks will remain closed in Tripura, Chandigarh, Jammu and Kashmir, Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh on October 26, 2026, for the respective regional observances of Laxmi Puja, Accession Day and Maharishi Valmiki’s birthday.Customers in the affected states should check with their respective branches before visiting, particularly if they have transactions that require in-person banking services.Banks will remain closed in Himachal Pradesh for Karva Chauth.Gujarat will see bank closures due to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birth anniversary.These holidays do not apply uniformly across the country. The applicable dates depend on the state and the regional observance listed for each location.In addition to festival-related holidays, scheduled and non-scheduled banks observe holidays on the second and fourth Saturdays of every month, as per the Reserve Bank of India’s holiday schedule.A bank holiday does not mean all banking services will stop. Customers can continue to use ATMs, Unified Payments Interface (UPI), internet banking and mobile banking applications for routine transactions, including fund transfers, bill payments and account management.However, services that require a physical branch visit may be affected on a holiday. Customers planning large cash deposits, cheque processing, demand drafts or other branch-dependent transactions may have to wait until their branch reopens.Checking the holiday calendar for the relevant state before making a branch visit can help customers plan transactions around the festive schedule and avoid unnecessary delays.
Article Summary: Banks will remain closed in Tripura, Chandigarh, Jammu and Kashmir, Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh on October 26, 2026. Customers planning large cash deposits, cheque processing, demand drafts or other branch-dependent transactions may have to wait until their branch reopens.

Article Title: Crude prices fall from six-month highs; WTI stands at $101 per barrel, Brent costs $115
Article Text:
Crude prcies fall from six month-highs, but trade beyond $100 per barrel

Strait of Hormuz remains a key concern

Supply measures fail to reverse the rally

Oil prices fell over 1% on Monday after surging to near six-month highs late last week. Despite the decline, prices remained elevated, with Brent crude hovering near $115 per barrel as continued attacks on Saudi Arabia kept concerns over global oil supplies alive.The US Federal Reserve's upcoming policy decision is another factor investors will watch as crude enters a potentially volatile week.WTI crude fell 1.71%, or $1.77, to $101.5 per barrel, while Brent crude declined 1.41%, or $1.65, to $115.1 per barrel.The decline followed a sharp rise on Friday, when prices settled nearly $3 higher after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia raised concerns about energy supplies. Brent recorded a 6% gain for the week, while WTI advanced 2.3%, taking prices close to six-month highs.The security situation remained tense over the weekend. The Houthis said they had attacked a Saudi airport and oil facilities on Saturday, while Saudi Arabia reported intercepting additional missiles and drones on Sunday. The country's main airport resumed partial operations the same day, following damage from an earlier round of Houthi attacks. The militant group has vowed to continue targeting the facility.Developments around the Strait of Hormuz and the security of energy infrastructure are expected to influence crude prices in the coming days. Brent has already crossed $117 per barrel, and analysts said any disruption to energy facilities or shipping through the strait could push global prices towards $120 per barrel. A credible move towards de-escalation, however, could lead to a sharp correction."The near-term bias remains bullish but highly headline-driven; traders should avoid chasing sharp rallies and monitor geopolitical developments, Fed guidance and weekly inventory data for directional confirmation," said Ajit Mishra, SVP - Research at Religare Broking.The latest price rally has been driven by escalating US-Iran tensions, fears of renewed military action, attacks on Saudi infrastructure and threats to important shipping routes, Mishra said. These developments have sustained the geopolitical risk premium in oil prices.Navneet Damani, head of research - commodities at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd, said, "The rally gathered pace as attention returned to escalating attacks around the Hormuz and Saudi Arabia, reviving concerns over energy infrastructure and export security."Further uncertainty has emerged from reports that the US and Israel had prepared plans to target Iranian energy infrastructure, including nuclear facilities near Natanz, after the US mid-term elections on November 3. Iran warned of repercussions if Washington and Tel Aviv launched an attack, adding to concerns in the market.Efforts to ease supply concerns have so far done little to bring prices down. The International Energy Agency has indicated its readiness to release more strategic stocks, while the G7's additional 100 million barrels largely involves accelerating an existing release programme. The first Russian diesel cargo bound for the US has also failed to reverse the upward trend.According to Damani, market participants are now looking for evidence that these measures will translate into meaningful additional supplies, rather than responding to announcements alone."Although crude flows through Hormuz have shown some recovery, elevated freight costs, constrained regional shipments and persistent security threats continue to undermine export reliability. With physical supply yet to normalise, the risk premium remains elevated, and the balance of risks continues to favour the upside, though credible progress towards de-escalation could still trigger sharp profit-taking," Damani added.The market will also track weekly US inventory estimates from the American Petroleum Institute and the US Energy Information Administration, alongside Cushing crude inventories. These figures could offer further direction as traders assess the state of supply.
Article Summary: WTI crude fell 1.71%, or $1.77, to $101.5 per barrel, while Brent crude declined 1.41% to $115.1 per barrel. The decline followed a sharp rise on Friday, when prices settled nearly $3 higher after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia raised concerns about energy supplies.

Article Title: Middle East conflict may end, but energy crisis will drag on: IEA chief explains
Article Text:
IEA's Birol does not expect energy markets to return to pre-war levels in 2027

Oil prices near $120 a barrel add to economic pressure

Winter demand and refinery maintenance threaten fuel supplies

Europe faces a difficult winter

With oil prices edging towards $120 a barrel and winter adding to concerns over fuel supplies, the global energy crisis could outlast the Iran war itself.International Energy Agency (IEA) executive director Fatih Birol has warned that energy markets are unlikely to return to their pre-war conditions in 2027, urging governments and businesses to put energy security first.Speaking at the Singapore International Energy Week conference on Monday, Birol said that the conflict, which began in late February, had upended expectations of a surplus in the energy market this year. Instead, disruptions to global energy flows have tightened supplies and pushed up oil benchmarks and refined fuel prices."I am afraid I don't see any credible pathway that the markets will go next year, where we were before this war has started," Birol said.He called on countries and companies to prepare for a prolonged period of uncertainty, with energy security taking priority while they also consider what comes next."So therefore, we all need to get prepared, taking the energy security as a number one priority in our government, business world, but without forgetting what is the next chapter for the countries and for companies that are all here today," he said.The pressure on oil markets has already been visible in prices.More Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia sent Brent crude futures soaring to $117 a barrel on Friday, their highest level in nearly six months. Prices eased to $115 per barrel on Monday but still remained about 59% above their pre-war level."Oil prices are flirting with $120 a barrel and the prices for products are even much higher," Birol said.While he declined to predict where oil prices would go next, he warned that costs at these levels were becoming a major burden for several economies."I can tell you that the current price of oil is, for some countries, for example in Europe, maybe not so high and affordable. But in many parts of the world, having almost $120 oil prices is having a major impact on trade deficits."Oil is not the only concern. As winter approaches, Birol is also worried about the availability and cost of refined products, particularly diesel, which is used for heating in parts of the West.Demand for diesel typically rises during the colder months, just as several refineries are scheduled to undergo maintenance, adding another pressure point for fuel markets."I am worried on top of that for refined products because we are entering...winter season. Some parts of the world, where typically diesel demand goes high and several refineries are going through maintenance period."Europe, meanwhile, faces a difficult winter on the gas front. Countries have decided to cut imports of Russian gas, while the Iran war has added to the strain by disrupting gas exports from Qatar and the United Arab Emirates."In Europe, we are facing a tough winter because European countries have decided to cut gas imports from Russia and with the additional problem now rising from the Iran war, namely Qatar and the Emirates not being able to export gas as they were before, will put significant pressure on gas markets."The energy crisis could also give nuclear power a fresh push. Birol expects a "strong comeback" for the sector as countries grapple with the current situation. The IEA's recent survey found that 90 gigawatts of nuclear power capacity was under construction, the highest level in the past four decades, he said.
Article Summary: IEA executive director Fatih Birol warns energy markets are unlikely to return to pre-war conditions in 2027. He urges governments and businesses to put energy security first. Winter demand and refinery maintenance threaten fuel supplies in Europe and the U.S.

Article Title: E100 cars get regulatory green light ahead of planned launches
Article Text:
Govt allows registration of flex-fuel vehicles running on 85% to 100% ethanol-blended petrol

NEW DELHI: Government on Monday notified a change in Central Motor Vehicles Rules, allowing flex-fuel vehicles that can run on upto 100% ethanol blended petrol. This comes barely months before some of the car manufacturers are set to launch their E100 models.An official said the amendments update the emission provisions by including E100 alongside E85. Officials said E85 and E100 are "intended only for vehicles specially designed and certified to use it and will not be applicable for other vehicles. Vehicles that use E20 or normal fuel can't use E85 or E100 fuel. This notification doesn't require owners of existing vehicles to switch to E85 or modify their vehicles either at present or in future. "Officials said Flex Fuel technology is used in countries such as Brazil and the US. These vehicles are specially designed to operate on a range of ethanol and petrol blends using a single tank fuel. Depending on the vehicle's design and certification, this range may extend to E85 or E100, a fuel predominantly consisting of ethanol.Officials also said that ethanol has lower fossil carbon footprint than conventional petrol and the use of higher ethanol blends can help reduce tailpipe emission of carbon monoxide (CO) and certain hydrocarbons. Greater ethanol use will also reduce dependence on import of crude oil.
Article Summary: Govt allows registration of flex-fuel vehicles running on 85% to 100% ethanol- blended petrol. This comes barely months before some of the car manufacturers are set to launch their E100 models. Vehicles that use E20 or normal fuel can't use E85 or E100 fuel.

Article Title: Vande Bharat sleeper services on Mumbai-Bengaluru, Delhi-Varanasi routes in next one week
Article Text:
Country’s second sleeper Vande Bharat likely from October 31 on Kashi-Delhi route

NEW DELHI: Railways will roll out two Vande Bharat sleeper train services on the Mumbai-Bengaluru and Delhi-Varanasi routes ine next one week as part of efforts to expand its premium overnight rail travel network.TOI has learnt that two pairs of the premium long-distance trains are scheduled for roll out. While Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper is scheduled for inauguration of October 31 (Sunday), the inaugural run on Delhi-Varanasi route is scheduled for November 1 (next Monday).At present, Vande Bharat Sleeper service is in regular operation between Guwahati and Kolkata.The Mumbai-Bengaluru route would connect two major economic centres, catering to business travellers and other passengers travelling between Maharashtra and Karnataka. The Delhi-Varanasi service would link the national capital with one of the country’s key religious and tourist destinations, with the potential to benefit pilgrims and other travellers.The Mumbai-Bengaluru service is expected to cover the journey in around 15–16 hours, while the Delhi-Varanasi service is planned as an overnight train via Prayagraj and Kanpur.
Article Summary: Railways will roll out two Vande Bharat sleeper train services on the Mumbai- Bengaluru and Delhi-Varanasi routes ine next one week. The inaugural run on Delhi- Varanasi route is scheduled for November 1 (next Monday) At present, Vande. Bharat Sleeper service is in regular operation between Guwahati and Kolkata.

As the festive season brings people together, mithai continues to hold a special place in the country’s celebrations.While traditional favourites remain timeless, festive gifting is also evolving. People are increasingly looking for options that combine familiar flavours with thoughtful presentation, variety and a more premium experience. Whether it is a family gathering, a festive visit, a wedding celebration or a corporate gesture, sweets have become a way to make occasions more personal and memorable.Bringing together this connection with Indian traditions and contemporary tastes is Meetha by Radisson, Radisson Hotel Group’s curated Indian sweets offering. With options designed for different occasions, Meetha brings together the familiarity of Indian mithai and the presentation expected from a premium gifting experience.This Diwali, Meetha by Radisson offers a wide selection of more than 40 signature and artisanal mithai. The range includes much-loved classics such as Kaju Katli, Mathura Peda, Badam Katli and Mysore Pak, alongside fusion creations like Biscoff Barfi, Nutella Sandwich, Red Velvet Cheese Laddoo and Coco Orange Barfi. Each sweet is made with premium ingredients and presented with the same care that goes into its preparationsFor the festive season, Meetha by Radisson has launched six new box designs suited to everything from family celebrations to corporate gifting. For those looking for something more special, the brand also offers bespoke luxury hampers that combine elegance with indulgence, making them ideal for gifting that feels personal and memorable.As India enters another season of celebrations, the tradition of sharing sweets remains a reminder that the most meaningful gifts are often those rooted in culture, connection and the joy of being together. With Meetha by Radisson, this enduring tradition finds a contemporary expression, making every box an opportunity to share a little sweetness.
