Article Title: GSTAT allows GST refund on cancelled air tickets
Article Text:
File photo: GSTAT rules GST on cancelled airline tickets refundable if the airline returns the fare and GST to passengers and has supporting documents.

NEW DELHI: GST paid on cancelled airline tickets can be claimed as a refund if the airline has returned both the fare and GST to the passengers and has supporting documents to prove it, a GST Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT) has ruled.Ruling in the case of Singapore Airlines v/s Kochi Commissioner of CGST & CE, Kochi, Ernakulam bench of GSTAT has decided that there is “sufficient evidence” to ensure that the refund of cancelled tickets has reached the respective passengers directly and there is “no passing” of the incidence of tax.The GSTAT directed the revenue department to process the refund claim of the airline within two weeks and make payment along with interest.The case relates to eight GST refund claims totalling Rs 45,92,528 by Singapore Airlines for the period between Oct 2019 and March 2021. During the period, owing to Covid-19, the airline had to cancel flights and returned fares and GST to passengers. However, it could not adjust the credit notes against output tax.The GST joint commissioner had earlier rejected the refund claims, following which the appellant approached the GSTAT.Setting aside the JC(A) order, GSTAT in its order dated Oct 16 said, “The appellant airline is eligible for refund of GST collected from passengers and paid by them to the GST department, but subsequently refunded the entire amount of fare, including GST, to the passengers, on account of cancellation of the flights due to the Covid-19 pandemic in terms of Hon’ble Supreme Court’s order. ”The GSTAT also concluded that the appellant has provided sufficient evidence to ensure that the refund of the cancelled tickets have reached the respective passenger. Rahul Shekhar, partner—indirect tax at Nangia Global, said the ruling is a positive development, as GST should not become a cost where a transaction is cancelled, and the tax collected is fully refunded to customers.
Article Summary: GST paid on cancelled airline tickets can be claimed as a refund if the airline has returned both the fare and GST to the passengers. The case relates to eight GST refund claims totalling Rs 45,92,528 by Singapore Airlines for the period between Oct 2019 and March 2021. The GST joint commissioner had earlier rejected the refund claims.

Article Title: ‘Trusting entrepreneurs key to India’s success’
Article Text:
File photo: Anil Agarwal

Turning into an entrepreneur over 50 years ago

First public listing for a group company

Going global...

The metals empire and more...

Management’s visions and style...

On changing business environment in India

MUMBAI: Anil Agarwal , the billionaire-entrepreneur with his origin in Patna in Bihar, is putting in place a plan that would see every Vedanta group company being managed by professionals, and not by any of his family members. The majority ownership of these companies, however, would remain with the group’s London-listed company in which the family has majority ownership. Agarwal has set a $100-billion market capitalisation target for the group companies together for the short term, up from about $55 billion now. And, he also wants at least 35% of the group’s workforce to be women, up from 22% now.Agarwal, who completed 50 years of his entrepreneurial journey this year, spoke to TOI. Excerpts:I came to Bombay (now Mumbai) from Patna in end-1975. In Patna, my father had a factory for iron grill gates and aluminium conductors. I worked there with him for five years and learnt the trade. In those days children in business families used to work from a very early age, alongside their studies. I started at 14.We listed Sterlite Cable and continued to grow the company. We started with cable, then set up a copper rod plant in Lonavala, and later set up a copper smelter in Tuticorin in the south. We used imported technology and machinery for these plants.That was the turning point.In 1989, we made our first attempt to settle abroad. We stayed in New York for four years but did not find much success. Then in 1991, the Narasimha Rao govt came to power in India. During his time, the licence raj was abolished. And in 1992-93, we came back to India, set up a jelly-filled cable factory, and there was a lot of growth. Then, in 1995, we acquired another factory in London, named Dura-Tube, for $3 million, ran it for a few years and then sold it for $7 million. After that, when we went to London, it took us three or four years.Currently, across the listed and unlisted entities, we have 10 major companies. We have very large operations in aluminium, copper, zinc, lead, silver and some other metals. We also have a very large renewable business. Our transmission business is also very strong.Our vision is that, given our present position, our market cap will reach $100 billion in about a year or two. And in the long term each of these companies have the potential to become $50–100 billion companies. As for the management style, professionals will run the companies on an incentive basis. Our foreign company, owned by the family, will hold 54% in each of the ten companies. There should be a legacy of building very good companies with strong rules and regulations. Another goal of mine is, across all our businesses women should constitute 35% of the workforce. At present, our group’s revenue is around $30 billion. In two years, it should be $50 billion. And over the next three years, we are investing $25 billion to expand what we are doing. It is a very large investment, and once this is completed, our overall capacity will more than double.India is a country where people are born entrepreneurs. The more you trust and support them, the more the country will progress and the more employment will be created. That is the key.
Article Summary: Anil Agarwal is putting in place a plan that would see every Vedanta group company being managed by professionals, and not by any of his family members. The majority ownership of these companies would remain with the group’s London- listed company in which the family has majority ownership. He has set a $100-billion market capitalisation target for the group companies together, up from about $55 billion now.

Article Title: Global AI companies turn to India for data centre capacity
Article Text:
File photo: AI companies are using Indian data centres to serve customers

BENGALURU: Global AI companies are using Indian data centres to serve customers overseas, not just local users, as delays in securing power and capacity elsewhere push them to spread their computing infrastructure across countries, operators told TOI.“We are already hosting some customers and have contracted large capacities with some of them,” said Sunil Gupta, co-founder, CEO and MD of Yotta Data Services, which operates data centres and rents out AI computing capacity.“We are seeing international AI customers use infrastructure hosted and operated from India to serve workloads beyond the country,” he said.At CtrlS Datacenters, which houses customers’ servers, discussions can begin with a requirement for 20 megawatts of capacity and quickly turn to expanding it to 100MW or more, said founder and CEO Sridhar Pinnapureddy. “AI is compressing the time available to respond while increasing the scale we need to build for. Higher power densities and advanced cooling must be planned alongside land, transmission, and future expansion,” he said.
Article Summary: Global AI companies are using Indian data centres to serve customers overseas, not just local users. Delays in securing power and capacity elsewhere push them to spread their computing infrastructure across countries. “We are seeing international AI customers use infrastructure hosted and operated from India to serve workloads beyond the country,” said Sunil Gupta, co-founder of Yotta Data Services.

Article Title: Deadlines to file annual statements, returns extended
Article Text:
File photo: Ministry of Corporate Affairs

NEW DELHI: The corporate affairs ministry has extended the deadline for companies to file their annual financial statements for the fiscal 2025-26 till Dec 31. Besides, they can submit their annual returns to the ministry till Jan 31, 2027, as per a circular. The extension of deadlines follows representations from stakeholders as they were facing issues in submitting the annual statutory filings through the MCA 21 portal.
Article Summary: The corporate affairs ministry has extended the deadline for companies to file their annual financial statements for the fiscal 2025-26 till Dec 31. Besides, they can submit their annual returns to the ministry till Jan 31, 2027, as per a circular.

Article Title: Dalal Street braces for volatile week
Article Text:
Geopolitical tensions and soaring crude prices are fuelling market volatility, weakening the rupee and driving foreign investors away from Indian stocks.

MUMBAI: Rising geopolitical risks, elevated crude oil prices, a weakening rupee and unabated foreign fund selling have combined to force Dalal Street investors on the back foot. As a result, markets are bracing for another volatile week. In addition to the above factors weighing on sentiment, there are talks of renewed military attacks on Iran by the US-Israel combine ahead of the crucial polls in the two countries where the incumbent heads of state are expected to face severe election setbacks.One of the highlights of the week would be the listing of Jio Platforms which on Friday closed the biggest IPO in India ever and is expected to list on Oct 28.As talks of an escalation in war in the Persian Gulf circulated, Brent crude prices jumped to above the $114 per barrel level on Friday and settled at about the $112 level, levels not seen since May this year. That also weakened the rupee which again inched closer to the 95-to-a-dollar level at close on Friday. The only positive for the week was that foreign funds were net buyers in two of the five sessions.During the week, foreign funds significantly reduced their selling and even turned buyers on two days, said VK Vijayakumar, the chief investment strategist at Geojit Investments.“The moderation in the US bond yields with the 10-year yield declining from 5.36% to around 5%, appreciation in the rupee to 94.94 to the dollar and the low valuations, particularly of the large-caps, contributed to the moderation in FII selling,” he said.Vijayakumar, however, pointed out that in Oct, net selling by foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) in stocks was Rs 53,337 crore while the corresponding figure for the year so far was Rs 3.7 lakh crore (excluding IPO proceeds), the highest ever yearly figure.Friday’s session also saw a sharp slide in midcap and smallcap stocks. And this could be due to forced liquidation in the margin-funded long positions in the market. For long, several of the top market players have been warning about the growing size of the margin trade funding (MTF) book that has doubled in the last two years to about Rs 1.5 lakh crore now.During midweek, Jio Platforms, after its hugely successful IPO of Rs 30,213 crore was subscribed over 22 times, will list on the bourses. In the unofficial market for yet-to-list stocks, speculators are betting on a listing price of about Rs 1,370, a 22% listing gain.
Article Summary: Rising geopolitical risks, elevated crude oil prices, a weakening rupee and unabated foreign fund selling have combined to force Dalal Street investors on the back foot. One of the highlights of the week would be the listing of Jio Platforms which on Friday closed the biggest IPO in India ever.

Article Title: West Asia crisis: Government ready with energy, fertiliser stocks
Article Text:
Govt has energy and fertiliser stocks ready, but higher oil and freight costs will strain the rupee, deficits and foreign investment.

NEW DELHI: As war clouds gather over West Asia once again, govt seems better prepared with energy and fertiliser stocks, but higher oil prices will hurt the currency and deficit levels, apart from foreign portfolio investment, which is already under strain.Besides, the already-elevated freight rates — nearly 10 times the pre-war level on certain routes — will spike further as insurance premiums rise in an environment when finding vessels and crew to go into the Strait of Hormuz is often difficult. This will have an impact on exports as well as the entire supply chain when container shortages are seen in the eastern hemisphere, along with port congestion in certain parts of the world.On Oct 22, the Drewry World Container Index was at $4,585 for a 40-feet container, compared with $1,746 on Oct 25, 2025.“It is already pushing freight rates beyond a point. Right now, buyers are managing because they were short of inventory. Now, that they are stocked up, it is unclear if they can absorb higher freight. Fresh disruption in West Asia will have an adverse impact for rest of the world too,” said Ajai Sahay, director general at Fieo.He said container rates to West Asian ports have shot up from $800 to $8,000 to $10,000 now.“The East-West container freight market remains uncertain. Security risks and attacks on ships continue to affect vessel movements through the Gulf, with only two containerships sailing into the Gulf in Week 42, down from five the previous week. Meanwhile, sailings through the Suez Canal increased slightly, from 54 in Week 41 to 55 in Week 42,” Drewry said.There are also concerns over crew and vessels entering the Strait of Hormuz, which has emerged as the epicentre of the conflict. In any case, most businesses reckon that any uncertainty, especially a war that has implications on global energy supplies, is best avoided.Oil is the biggest concern with crude price for Indian refiners averaging $120 a barrel in Oct, the highest monthly average in 12 years. And, with petrol averaging $140 a barrel and diesel at over $154, the pressure on state-run retailers in mounting as they incur losses, given that pump prices are linked to the import price of the product.Although govt had shielded them through duty cuts and permission to raise prices subsequently, the Centre has limited headroom for fiscal concessions. Already, fuel and fertiliser subsidies are well past last year’s level and it will have to provide extra, if the need arises.For the moment, top officials said, fertiliser companies took advantage of a falling price window to stock up for the next season and the fertiliser ministry had some surplus cash with it due to the savings.There is some cushion for the Centre due to higher-than-budgeted disinvestment receipts and dividends from state-run financial institutions and RBI, with tax collections holding up so far, which is expected to keep the fiscal deficit within the target of 4.3% of GDP. But, a spike in the import bill due to higher commodity prices will have impact on the trade deficit and the current account deficit. And, a weaker rupee will make it less attractive for foreign funds to invest in Indian stocks.
Article Summary: Oil is the biggest concern with crude price for Indian refiners averaging $120 a barrel in Oct, the highest monthly average in 12 years. There are also concerns over crew and vessels entering the Strait of Hormuz, which has emerged as the epicentre of the conflict.

Article Title: France’s economic woes: Debt nears 122% of GDP, growth forecast at just 0.4%
Article Text:
France’s debt, taxes and borrowing costs rise as economic growth slows

France’s public debt nears 122% of GDP

Government spending accounts for 57.2% of GDP

France faces higher borrowing costs

France’s growth forecast falls to 0.4%

France is facing mounting pressure on two fronts: growing public anger over the cost of living and an economy struggling with high debt, taxes and weak growth. Student protests that began with school blockades have spread, turning violent, putting the spotlight on the country’s economic troubles and deepening political tensions.The rising cost of living is one of the concerns behind the demonstrations, which began largely peacefully but disrupted schools before escalating into wider unrest and pockets of violence involving young people on Saturday. The issue is not unique to France, but it comes at a difficult time for the country’s economy.France is also struggling to bring its public finances under control. Carsten Brzeski, global chief of macro at ING bank, said “France is not Greece”, referring to the financial crisis that shook the European Union in 2009. However, France has repeatedly failed to meet its targets for spending, economic growth and cost-cutting.With President Emmanuel Macron nearing the end of his nearly decade-long tenure, the state of the country’s finances is also expected to be a key issue in the race to succeed him next spring.France’s public debt stood at nearly 3.6 trillion euros (nearly $4.08 trillion) at the end of June, equivalent to 119% of its gross domestic product (GDP).The government has warned that the figure could rise further. Three weeks ago, it said the budget would again exceed European Union spending limits, with public debt expected to reach nearly 122% of GDP, setting a new record, AP reported.The growing debt leaves the government with difficult choices. It needs to reduce spending or raise taxes, which are already among the highest in Europe.Gilbert Cette, an economics professor at Neoma Business School in Paris, described the debt as “enormous”, saying, “France’s entire economic policy is constrained by such a sizable debt level.”Cette said France had shown “talent” in both increasing government spending and cutting taxes in recent years, making it harder to get public finances back on track.Brzeski also warned that France’s approach to economic reforms was affecting its credibility. Writing last week, he said, “Greece’s credibility was destroyed by false statistics; France’s is being eroded by false promises and the inability or unwillingness to start fiscal and structural reforms,”High government spending is another challenge for France. In 2025, public expenditure accounted for 57.2% of the country’s economic output, according to Eurostat, the European Union’s statistics agency. The EU average was just under 50%.A large share of this spending goes towards healthcare, pensions and subsidies for businesses. With government expenditure already making up such a large part of the economy, reducing it further would require difficult decisions.France also has one of the highest tax burdens in the European Union. Tax revenue and social contributions accounted for 45.2% of GDP in 2024, putting the country a close second behind Denmark, according to Eurostat. The EU average was just over 40%.This leaves the government with limited room to raise taxes further to reduce the deficit. Cutting spending is another option, but it would mean making choices about areas that already account for a significant share of the economy.The cost of borrowing is adding to the pressure on France’s public finances. The yield on its 10-year government bond stood at 4.96% as of Tuesday.Higher bond yields mean the government has to pay more to borrow money. This can leave less room in the budget for other priorities, including pensions, education, healthcare, defence and social programmes.Germany, the European Union’s largest economy, faces lower borrowing costs. Its equivalent 10-year government bond, known as the Bund, had a yield of about 3.4%.The gap between French and German 10-year bond yields has widened, highlighting the difference in borrowing costs between the two countries. This adds to the challenges facing France as it tries to manage its debt and spending.France’s economic outlook remains weak. The International Monetary Fund has forecast growth of just 0.4% for the country this year, the lowest rate among developed economies.The forecast is well below the expected growth rates for both the global economy and advanced economies. Global output is projected to grow by 3.1% this year, while advanced economies are expected to expand by 2.1%.France’s projected growth is around one-third of Germany’s forecast rate and half of Italy’s. Japan, which has the second-lowest growth forecast among developed countries, is expected to grow by 0.7%.Slow growth makes it harder for France to manage its public finances while dealing with high debt, substantial government spending and an already heavy tax burden. Rising borrowing costs further add to the pressure.With the economy growing slowly and public finances under strain, France faces difficult choices over how to control its debt and spending. These economic challenges are unfolding alongside political divisions and protests over the cost of living, while the state of public finances is set to remain an important issue ahead of next spring’s presidential succession race.
Article Summary: France’s public debt stood at nearly 3.6 trillion euros (nearly $4.08 trillion) at the end of June, equivalent to 119% of its gross domestic product (GDP) The government has warned that the figure could rise further, with public debt expected to reach nearly 122% of GDP. High government spending is another challenge for France. In 2025, public expenditure accounted for 57.2% of the country's economic output, according to Eurostat.

Article Title: US Fed expected to hold rates as inflation, energy costs weigh ahead of midterms
Article Text:
US Fed expected to hold interest rates steady despite persistent inflation (representative image)

Inflation pressures complicate Fed's rate decision

Former Fed official says economic data favour further hikes

Trump's criticism of Fed independence

The US Federal Reserve is widely expected to keep interest rates unchanged at its meeting next week, despite persistent inflation and market expectations of at least one more rate hike before the end of the year, according to analysts cited by news agency AFP.The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) will meet over two days, with its interest rate decision scheduled for 2 pm local time (1800 GMT) on Wednesday.At its September meeting, the Fed raised its benchmark federal funds rate for the first time in three years, taking the target range to 3.75%-4%. The central bank has struggled to bring inflation down to its long-term target of 2%, which it has missed for more than five years.The decision comes just days before the November 3 US midterm elections, in which Democrats are seeking to wrest control of both chambers of Congress from President Donald Trump's Republican Party.The Fed's preferred inflation gauge, the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, reached a pandemic-era peak of 7.2% in 2022 before a series of interest rate increases brought it down to around 2.2% by late 2024.However, inflation subsequently rose again amid Trump's economic policies, including tariffs that disrupted global trade and the US war with Iran. The PCE index reached a three-year high of 3.9% in May.Since the US and Israel attacked Iran in late February, global energy prices have surged, with retaliatory actions by Tehran sharply restricting oil and gas supplies through the Gulf. Higher energy costs have also begun feeding into the prices of other goods and services, putting affordability at the forefront of concerns ahead of the midterm elections.The Fed faces the challenge of controlling inflation while supporting the labour market. Higher interest rates increase borrowing costs, potentially slowing economic activity and curbing price pressures, but they can also weigh on employment.The US economy has also been dealing with weakening consumer confidence and signs of stress in an otherwise resilient jobs market. The latest consumer confidence survey from the Conference Board was expected to show a further decline in October after confidence fell in September to its lowest level in more than a decade.Loretta Mester, a former president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland, told AFP that the timing of the meeting ahead of the elections would not influence policymakers' decision."The Fed doesn't take into account any kind of political issues in that FOMC room," she said. "It really is based on the economics."Mester argued that economic conditions supported further monetary tightening, pointing to a stable labour market and inflation remaining above the central bank's target."The data that's come in continue to show a stable labor market and continue to show inflation above target," she said, adding that there was no evidence of inflation moving towards the target."The economics would suggest then you need to continue raising rates."However, Mester said most policymakers appeared reluctant to move too quickly. She expected the Fed could hold rates steady in October and consider another increase at its next meeting in early December.Wendy Edelberg, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, also said that central bankers would prefer to avoid becoming part of the political debate ahead of the elections."It's unhelpful for everyone if the Fed gets wrapped up in all the political discourse right before an election," she said.Edelberg added that raising rates in December rather than October would have limited economic implications.She viewed a possible delay less as a concession to Trump, who has repeatedly called for lower interest rates, and more as a way for the Fed to avoid becoming a target of political criticism.Trump has repeatedly criticised the Federal Reserve over interest rates, which he considers too high. However, he has so far refrained from directing similar criticism at Kevin Warsh, whom he appointed to succeed Jerome Powell as Fed chair.Since returning to power last year, Trump has mounted an unprecedented challenge to the central bank's independence. His administration launched a criminal investigation into Powell and attempted to remove Fed Governor Lisa Cook.The investigation into Powell was dropped to smooth the way for Warsh's confirmation by the Senate, while the legal battle over Cook's removal continued despite a Supreme Court decision nullifying an earlier attempt to dismiss her.Last week, Cook declined to attend a hearing in a White House investigation into mortgage fraud allegations, which she denies.Meanwhile, the Fed's rate decision will come during a busy week for US economic data.Investors and policymakers were also awaiting updates on inflation, consumer confidence and third-quarter economic growth, alongside earnings reports from major companies.
Article Summary: US Federal Reserve is widely expected to keep interest rates unchanged at its meeting next week. The central bank has struggled to bring inflation down to its long-term target of 2%. The decision comes just days before the November 3 US midterm elections, in which Democrats are seeking to wrest control of both chambers of Congress.

Article Title: From fuel price hikes to cost-of-living concerns, US consumer sentiment nears record low
Article Text:
File photo: A shopper looks at the section of a grocery store in Fort Worth, Texas (Picture credit: AP)

Independent voters report weaker sentiment

Inflation expectations remain elevated

Federal Reserve decision due next week

US consumer sentiment edged down to near a record low in October as rising prices linked to the Middle East conflict weighed on households' views of the economy, a University of Michigan survey showed on Friday, with affordability emerging as a key issue ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.The university's Consumer Sentiment Index slipped to 48.0 this month from a final reading of 48.1 in September.Economists polled by Reuters had expected a reading of 46.3, which was also the preliminary estimate for October.October's reading was the second-lowest on record, following the all-time low of 44.8 recorded in May, shortly after the Iran war began."Purchasing power continues to dominate consumer views of the economy," said Joanne Hsu, director of the Surveys of Consumers. "Sentiment is now 10% below a year ago and 15% less than February, just prior to the Iran conflict."The survey's findings coincided with political polling showing that voters held a dim view of the economy and President Donald Trump's and the Republican Party's handling of it, Reuters reported.Millions of Americans have already cast early ballots ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, which will determine control of Congress for the final two years of Trump's term.Polls indicated Republicans were likely to lose control of the House of Representatives, with the Senate also potentially at stake. Trump's approval rating in a Reuters/Ipsos poll stood at a record low, amid a surge in fuel prices following his decision to attack Iran in late February.The University of Michigan survey found that the decline in sentiment was driven by respondents who identified as independents, a group that includes swing voters.Their sentiment score fell to 42.4 in October from 47.7 in September, putting it just above May's record low of 40.6. Sentiment scores among Democrats and Republicans improved.The survey also found that more independents and Republicans were citing high prices as a strain on their personal finances. Since January, the number of independents reporting inflation pressures as a financial burden had risen by 27%, while the figure among Republicans had increased by 52%. Among Democrats, the increase was 15%.Households with little or no exposure to the stock market had also increasingly cited high prices as a financial burden compared with the beginning of the year. The stock market had recently climbed rapidly amid enthusiasm for investments in artificial intelligence.The survey's measure of consumers' expectations for inflation over the next 12 months rose to 4.7% in October from 4.6% in September. The measure had stood at 3.4% in February, before the US-Israeli war with Iran began.Expectations for inflation over the next five years increased to 3.5% from 3.4% in September and 3.2% in March, shortly after the conflict began.In an accompanying report, Hsu said persistently elevated inflation expectations in the period following the Covid-19 pandemic posed a risk to the Federal Reserve's efforts to bring inflation down to its 2% target. The target had remained unmet for more than five years, she wrote."Consumers broadly expect inflation to accelerate, and this year’s increases in inflation expectations are not limited to one part of the political spectrum," Hsu said.She also cautioned that relatively resilient consumer spending, despite negative views of the economy, required close attention. If households were spending now to avoid expected price increases in the future, bringing inflation down could become more difficult, she added.Federal Reserve officials are scheduled to meet in Washington next week. Despite recent inflation readings that came in higher than expected, they were broadly expected to keep the policy interest rate unchanged at 3.75%-4.00%.The Fed had raised the rate by a quarter of a percentage point in September. Most officials had indicated a need for higher interest rates, while key policymakers had also expressed willingness to wait for more data before making their next move.
Article Summary: Consumer Sentiment Index slipped to 48.0 this month from a final reading of 48.1 in September. October's reading was the second-lowest on record, following the all-time low of 44.8 recorded in May, shortly after the Iran war began. More independents and Republicans were citing high prices as a strain on their personal finances.

Article Title: Trump eases tariffs on Canadian imports weeks before US midterms, offering relief to Maine
Article Text:
The new measures will take effect on October 30.

Collins seeks relief for Maine businesses

Trade tensions strain US-Canada ties

US President Donald Trump’s administration has eased some tariffs on Canadian imports, with the move coming just two weeks before the November 3 midterm elections. The decision could benefit Republican Senator Susan Collins, who is facing a tough re-election contest in Maine, a state whose economy has been affected by the trade dispute with Canada.The White House said the changes would remove tariffs on certain products, including "plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment". However, the administration will also introduce tariffs on other goods, including carpets, certain valves and waste products. The new measures will take effect on October 30.Collins said she had "secured" the exemptions for products important to Maine's agricultural sector, including blueberry, potato, apple and seaweed producers.Collins, who faces a strong challenge from a Democratic candidate, said farmers in her state depend on supplies from Canada that are difficult or expensive to source elsewhere.She said many farmers "rely on specialized equipment, packaging materials, and other products from Canada that are either unavailable from American suppliers or cannot be replaced without incurring significant expense."The senator's intervention comes as Democrats target her seat in their bid to take control of Congress from Republicans in the November 3 midterm elections.Maine shares a border with Canada, and businesses in the state have felt the effects of Trump's trade policies.The partial tariff relief could ease costs for some businesses, although the introduction of duties on other Canadian products means the changes will not benefit every sector.Also Read: After renaming Lake Ontario, Google CEO rejects US request to rename Atlantic Ocean The United States and Canada have closely connected economies, with roughly 70 per cent of Canadian exports going to the US. Trade relations have deteriorated since negotiations between the two countries broke down in August, prompting Trump to impose a fresh round of tariffs.Earlier US duties on Canadian cars, steel, aluminium and lumber have hurt businesses, contributed to job losses and weighed on economic growth. Canada entered a technical recession this year after its economy contracted for two consecutive quarters.The tariffs imposed after the collapse of trade talks affected goods worth around $20 billion, equivalent to 5.5 per cent of Canadian exports to the US. The targeted products ranged from hockey sticks to cement.Since returning to office for his second term, Trump has imposed extensive tariffs on imports from both allies and rivals, arguing that other countries have taken advantage of the United States.His administration has also linked some threatened tariffs to broader political and foreign policy goals.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump’s administration has eased some tariffs on Canadian imports. The move comes just two weeks before the November 3 midterm elections. The decision could benefit Republican Senator Susan Collins, who is facing a tough re-election contest in Maine. The new measures will take effect on October 30.

Article Title: Two critical PHP flaws trigger global alert; millions of services face cyber risk
Article Text:
Two critical PHP flaws trigger global alert.

India ranked ninth globally among services displaying PHP information.

BENGALURU: Two critical PHP vulnerabilities that could allow hackers to remotely execute code on servers without authentication have triggered a cybersecurity alert, potentially exposing millions of internet-facing services. In a separate advisory, PHP also urged users to temporarily disable a file-upload tracking feature to mitigate another remote code execution risk, adding to concerns over the widely used programming language.PHP advised users on Oct 23 to temporarily disable its session upload progress feature until the next regular bugfix release. The warning followed an earlier advisory on Oct 21 about a related vulnerability. The latest issue affects applications only when specific session settings are changed while running and the upload progress feature remains enabled. Users who have already disabled the feature do not need to take further action.The broader concerns centre on two critical vulnerabilities collectively referred to as PHP2Shell. Aamir Lakhani, global director of threat intelligence and adversarial artificial intelligence research at Fortinet, said: “Two critical PHP vulnerabilities disclosed this week pose an urgent security and business continuity risk for organizations that depend on websites, customer portals, and other web applications.PHP is a server-side programming language used by widely deployed platforms such as WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and Magento. Companies can be exposed through commercial applications, hosting providers and embedded software components even if they do not develop PHP applications themselves.The potential scale of exposure is significant. Censys identified approximately 36.7 million internet-facing services reporting potentially affected PHP versions in its Oct 22 snapshot. These are service counts, not unique servers or organisations, and may include installations already patched through vendor updates.Saeed Abbasi, head of the Threat Research Unit and director of product at Qualys, said the company found 167 million PHP package installations across 12,000 organisations, with 73% deployed on internet-facing assets, putting them within reach of remote attackers. “Applying a patch alone will not be sufficient for systems running unsupported versions, where upgrading is the only viable long-term solution. The key takeaway is that nearly all PHP installations are either vulnerable or running unsupported versions,” he said.CloudSEK said Shodan identified 2.2 million internet-facing services displaying PHP information worldwide, with India ranking ninth at 53,400 services. Of 36,700 Indian services revealing their PHP versions, about 36,100 were unpatched, including 19,500 running versions that have reached end of life, said Akash Karthi, a security researcher at CloudSEK.
Article Summary: Two critical PHP vulnerabilities that could allow hackers to remotely execute code on servers without authentication have triggered a cybersecurity alert. In a separate advisory, PHP urged users to temporarily disable a file-upload tracking feature to mitigate another remote code execution risk. The broader concerns centre on two critical vulnerabilities collectively referred to as PHP2Shell.

Article Title: Amex to cut 3,500 jobs globally despite raising 2026 profit forecast
Article Text:
American Express announced it will be laying off around 3,500 employees worldwide

American Express is cutting about 5 percent of its global workforce, affecting around 3,500 employees, as chief executive officer Steve Squeri seeks to control rising expenses and streamline operations, even as the company raises its full-year earnings forecast after reporting better-than-expected third-quarter results.According to Bloomberg, Squeri told Bloomberg TV that the company has around 78,000 employees globally. Speaking during a call with analysts on Friday, he said the job cuts were aimed at making the company more agile and efficient by reducing management layers and speeding up decision-making.The move comes amid a broader wave of workforce reductions across the financial services sector, with companies seeking to improve efficiency and, in some cases, citing the growing use of artificial intelligence.Barclays said this week it would eliminate 5,000 jobs, while HSBC is planning reductions across its UK wealth-management business. Citigroup has also been reducing its workforce.Amex announced the cuts after reporting adjusted earnings of $4.68 per share for the third quarter, beating the average analyst estimate of $4.49 in a Bloomberg survey. The company also raised its full-year 2026 earnings forecast to between $18.30 and $18.60 per share, from its earlier projection of $17.30 to $17.90.However, the company's billed business, which measures transactions on its credit cards and other products, came in at $454 billion during the quarter, below the average analyst estimate of $456.9 billion. Amex said it had exited certain small-business co-brand deals, affecting the results.Analysts at Truist Securities, including Brian Foran, described the results as mixed, noting that the earnings beat and improved guidance were positive but that slower growth in billed business was a disappointment.The company reported third-quarter expenses of $14.5 billion, an increase of about 9 percent, although the figure was below analysts' estimate of $14.8 billion. Rising costs have added to the pressure on management to improve operational efficiency while sustaining business growth.Amex's results were also affected by the sale of its equity interest in Global Business Travel Group Inc, which generated an after-tax gain of $751 million. The company used part of the proceeds to fund a $253 million after-tax restructuring charge linked to efficiency initiatives. The gain, net of the restructuring charge, was excluded from adjusted results.“Our business momentum continues, with strength in billings, new acquisitions and card member retention, and excellent credit quality,” Squeri said in a statement.The company has also been investing in its premium-card offerings. Last year, it introduced several new benefits for its Platinum card, and earlier this month announced a partnership with Airbnb that will allow certain luxury rentals booked through its travel site to qualify for cardholders' annual lodging credit.Chief financial officer Christophe Le Caillec had previously said marketing expenses were expected to rise by around 10 percent in the second half of 2026 compared with the same period last year.Separately, Amex faces a $350 million fine following enforcement actions by the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and the Federal Reserve over alleged deficiencies in its anti-money-laundering systems. The company said the penalty would not affect its previously issued full-year 2026 earnings guidance or its 2027 outlook. The regulatory orders also do not impose an asset cap on the company.
Article Summary: Amex announced the cuts after reporting adjusted earnings of $4.68 per share for the third quarter. Chief executive officer Steve Squeri said the job cuts were aimed at making the company more agile and efficient by reducing management layers. The move comes amid a broader wave of workforce reductions across the financial services sector.

Article Title: PHP security flaws trigger global scramble; CERT-In flags vulnerabilities
Article Text:
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a criticalseverity warning. (Reuters photo)

CERT-In Flags Vulnerabilities

BENGALURU: It has been a difficult day for cybersecurity, with critical vulnerabilities in PHP triggering an urgent global patching effort, millions of reported hacking attempts, and precautionary shutdowns of some online services. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual, remarking at an event in Cologne in Germany that he had not seen anything like it “in a long, long time”.The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP, a widely used open-source scripting language that powers websites and web applications. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely, disclose memory and potentially compromise affected systems.In its advisory issued on Wednesday, CERT-In said reports had confirmed large-scale exploitation in the wild and urged organisations and individuals using affected versions to apply security updates urgently.Google Cloud executives Chris Betz, chief information security officer, and Raluca Ada Popa, head of Gemini Security at Google DeepMind, said PHP and cybersecurity firm Wiz Research disclosed the two vulnerabilities after research that used multiple AI models to identify and help remediate them.Google Cloud said its own infrastructure was not vulnerable, but warned that customers running PHP applications on the platform could be exposed. It urged customers to update their applications to patched PHP versions and redeploy them. Google is also rolling out updated serverless base images for supported PHP runtimes, with automatic updates available for certain services and configurations.The scale of the response has extended beyond India. “In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it,” Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince wrote in a post on X on Wednesday. Companies and govt agencies in several countries temporarily restricted access to some online services as a precaution while they worked to secure vulnerable systems.Cloudflare’s blog said it successfully deployed mitigations for all its customers after the PHP vulnerabilities were leaked before their official disclosure date. The company observed attack traffic targeting customers and tracked how attackers modified their payloads to try to bypass its security.
Article Summary: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely, disclose memory and potentially compromise affected systems. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual.

Article Title: Barclays to slash 5,000 jobs by 2026-end as AI takes on bigger role in bank's operations
Article Text:
Barclays to slash 5,000 jobs

Barclays plans to eliminate around 5,000 jobs, or 5% of its global workforce, by the end of this year as the British lender streamlines its operations and increases its investment in technology, including artificial intelligence (AI).The bank has already closed 1,000 positions and expects to cut another 4,000. Around 60% of the reductions are expected to affect support functions, including developers, while operational and functional roles will account for most of the job losses.The move comes as Barclays approaches the end of a three-year cost-cutting programme focused primarily on its UK retail banking business. Its investment banking division is also affected.In its third-quarter earnings presentation on Thursday, the bank said it was “structurally reducing the cost base to generate capacity for investment.” It described the expected outcome as “organisational simplification and technology change efficiency driven by AI.”Barclays said AI was the "icing on the cake" of its wider modernisation strategy. Group chief executive CS Venkatakrishnan said the job cuts reflected significant investment in technology to simplify and improve the business.Barclays reported pre-tax profit of £2.3 billion ($3.1 billion) for the three months to September, up 12% from the same period a year earlier. The figure matched forecasts compiled by LSEG, although the results were also described as slightly below forecast.Group income stood at £7.4 billion, below analysts' estimate of £7.61 billion, while net interest income was broadly unchanged at £3.91 billion.The bank's CET1 capital ratio, a measure of financial solvency, edged down to 14.2% from 14.3% at the end of the second quarter. Return on tangible equity fell to 11.7% from 16.1%.Barclays shares were almost 1% lower less than an hour into the trading session. Economists are examining company results for evidence that spending on new technology, particularly AI, is improving day-to-day operations, boosting efficiency and reducing staffing requirements.Barclays' latest workforce reduction comes amid this wider scrutiny of how companies are using AI and whether the technology is delivering operational gains.
Article Summary: Barclays plans to eliminate around 5,000 jobs, or 5% of its global workforce, by the end of this year. The bank has already closed 1,000 positions and expects to cut another 4,000. Around 60% of the reductions are expected to affect support functions.

Article Title: Meta Q3 results: Net income jumps 264% to $9.86 billion, but legal charge hits operating income
Article Text:
Meta's Q3 net income jumps 264% to $9.86 billion

Higher spending planned for AI infrastructure

Meta Platforms' net income more than tripled in the third quarter of 2026, rising 264 per cent year-on-year to $9.86 billion, as higher advertising revenue boosted its financial performance. However, a $9.89 billion legal charge pushed operating income down 37 per cent despite a 26 per cent increase in overall revenue.The company's revenue reached $64.60 billion in the quarter ended September 30, compared with $51.24 billion in the same period last year. Net income stood at $2.71 billion a year earlier, while diluted earnings per share rose to $3.83 from $1.05.Advertising remained the biggest contributor to Meta's revenue, bringing in $63.06 billion, up 26 per cent from a year ago. The number of ad impressions across its family of applications increased 10 per cent, while the average price per advertisement rose 14 per cent year-on-year.Despite the increase in revenue and net income, operating income dropped to $12.99 billion from $20.54 billion in the year-ago quarter. Total costs and expenses climbed 68 per cent to $51.61 billion, reflecting, among other expenses, a $9.89 billion charge tied to an agreement with 52 US state attorneys general to resolve litigation concerning teen mental health and social media.Meta said that excluding this charge, operating income would have been $22.88 billion. Diluted earnings per share would have reached $7.40, rather than the reported $3.83.Meta expects revenue in the fourth quarter to be between $73 billion and $76 billion. It has also revised its full-year 2026 expense outlook upwards to $175-179 billion, taking the legal charge into account.The company has increased its capital expenditure forecast for 2026 to $135-145 billion, from the previous range of $130-145 billion. The spending is part of its continued investment in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure and other business priorities.In the chief financial officer's outlook commentary, Meta said, “Our AI investments are already delivering substantial incremental advertising revenue through stronger engagement, better recommendations, and more efficient monetization.”The company said its spending on AI models and infrastructure was opening up additional revenue opportunities. However, it expects these investments to take longer to generate returns than its core business.“While these investments will take longer to generate returns than those in our core business, the breadth of monetization opportunities and internal efficiencies gives us confidence in their long-term potential,” the commentary said.Meta expects its AI investments, improvements in its models and new product launches to support strong overall revenue growth through 2027.The company is still working on its budget and capacity plans for next year as it continues to invest in AI infrastructure and pursue the revenue opportunities it expects these investments to create.
Article Summary: Meta Platforms' Q3 net income jumps 264% to $9.86 billion. Company's revenue reached $64.60 billion in the quarter ended September 30, compared with $51.24 billion in same period last year. Advertising remained the biggest contributor to Meta's revenue, bringing in $63.06 billion, up 26% from a year ago.

Article Title: Brent crude tops $110 as fresh attacks in Saudi Arabia raise concerns over oil supplies
Article Text:
Crude prices hold above $110 per barrel

Shipping risks extend beyond Strait of Hormuz

US crude inventories fall, distillate stocks rise

Oil prices edged higher on Thursday, with Brent crude trading above $110 a barrel. The rise came after fresh Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia prompted US to order some diplomats and their family members to leave American missions in the Kingdom.At the same time, concerns over shipping safety and oil supplies in the region also persisted.WTI crude was trading at $98.05, up 90 cents or 0.93%, while Brent crude stood at $110, up $1.15 or 1.06%.US officials told Reuters that the state department also plans to withdraw family members from several other American missions in the region.The latest security concerns followed a series of attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis on Wednesday. At least one person was killed and eight others wounded in an attack on a civilian airport in Dammam. A drone attack on a Saudi oil field killed two people.Explosions were also reported in Sirik, in southern Iran, on Wednesday. Iranian media said that the nature and origin of the blasts were unknown.The threat to energy supplies has extended to maritime routes beyond the Strait of Hormuz. Kpler data showed at least 18 attacks on shipping over the past two weeks.LSEG analysts warned that Iran was targeting tankers further afield, including in the Gulf of Oman. Such attacks were jeopardising Gulf crude loadings and ship-to-ship transfers that support regional loadings.Iran's leadership also issued fresh statements amid the tensions. Foreign minister Abbas Araqchi told the Financial Times on Wednesday that Iran was fully prepared to defend itself. President Masoud Pezeshkian told state media that the US could not expect dialogue while blockading and threatening Iran.US crude inventories declined by 3.06 million barrels last week to 412.5 million barrels, according to data released by the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) on Wednesday. The fall was greater than the 820,000-barrel draw expected by analysts in a Reuters poll.Distillate inventories, which include diesel and heating oil, increased by 1.68 million barrels to 104.3 million barrels during the week. Analysts had expected these stockpiles to fall by 1.16 million barrels, EIA data showed.Separately, the Trump administration is offering to loan up to nearly a third of the US emergency heating oil reserve, which holds one million barrels. The department of energy announced the move on Wednesday as the administration seeks to contain prices that have risen amid diesel shortages linked to the wars in Iran and Ukraine.Elsewhere, Russian President Vladimir Putin met US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg on Wednesday to discuss ending the war in Ukraine. The meeting came as Washington renewed efforts to end Europe's bloodiest conflict since World War Two.The Kremlin said Putin had agreed to resume US-mediated peace talks with Ukraine as soon as next month. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy backed the proposed talks and said he hoped they would begin as soon as possible.
Article Summary: WTI crude was trading at $98.05, up 90 cents or 0.93%, while Brent crude stood at $110, up $1.15 or 1.06%. US state department also plans to withdraw family members from several other American missions in the region. Latest security concerns followed a series of attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis on Wednesday.
